title: NeurocrItical Care Unit - BundlE ApproaCh fOr individualized Nutrition
summary: In the context of the study, the treatment outcomes of neurointensive care patients are being compared. A prospectively collected cohort before the change in clinical nutrition practice is compared with a prospectively collected cohort afterward (pre-/post-design).

interventions.name:
(Pre change in clinical managemant)
- Resting energy expenditure (REE) using the Mifflin-St Jeor formula.
70% of REE for the first 0-72 hours; >72 hours, 100% of REE.
- Protein intake 1.5 g/kg body weight
- Parenteral nutrition in cases of contraindications for enteral nutrition or inadequate ca

(Post change in clinical management)
- Resting energy expenditure (REE) using the Harris-Benedict equation or indirect calorimetry
- 50% of REE for the first 0-24 hours; 70% of REE for 25-72 hours; >72 hours, 100% of REE, considering individual metabolic tolerance (glucose and phosphate metabolism

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Neurological condition as the reason for admission to the intensive care unit
- Expected length of stay exceeding 10 days
- Inclusion within the first 48 hours after admission
- Enteral or parenteral nutrition
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous stays in an intensive care unit for more than one day
- Pre-existing muscle disease
- Tetra- or paraplegia existing prior to admission
